name: Cottontail Rabbit
description: a brown rabbit, white tail flashing

knowledgeLevels.1: Cottontail rabbit. Brown, white tail. Fast.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean), hide (warm), bones (tools). Gut quickly.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: protein, but lean (rabbit starvation if only food). Need fat too.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: snare on runs (not random). Check at dawn/dusk. Cook with fat.

unknown: a brown blur with a white tail-flag, freezing between hops
behaviorDesc: Freezes, then bolts in a zigzag. Fast but predictable — it runs in a straight line after the first juke.
huntText: It freezes. You hold your breath. Then — white tail flashing — it bolts!
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean meat, one good meal. All protein, no fat: eat it with something greasy or you’ll run hollow (rabbit starvation is real).
tell: locks mid-hop, one ear swiveling toward you.
diseaseVector: Rabbits carry tularemia — wear gloves gutting, and cook it through. Ticks ride them too.

name: Gray Squirrel
description: a gray squirrel, chattering

knowledgeLevels.1: Gray squirrel. Quick, noisy.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (small), hide (gloves). Hard to skin (small).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: decent fat in fall. Good stew meat.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: hunt in fall (fat). Use a sling or trap. They follow patterns.

unknown: a gray flicker in the branches, chattering
behaviorDesc: Stays in trees. Drops to grab nuts, then spirals up the trunk. You need to catch it on the ground.
huntText: It chatters at you from the branch — scolding, not scared. Then it drops, grabs, and spirals up before you move.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — small, but a fall squirrel carries fat. Stew meat; the hide makes gloves if you’re patient.
tell: goes silent mid-chatter, tail flicking hard.
diseaseVector: Squirrels carry ticks and fleas. Cook the meat through.

name: White-tailed Deer
description: a deer, white tail raised in alarm

knowledgeLevels.1: White-tailed deer. Large. Dangerous if cornered.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lots), hide (clothing), bones (tools), antlers (weapons).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: feeds many. Fat is crucial. Organs are vitamin-rich (eat first).
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: need a weapon or deadfall. Track by prints. Gut immediately. Hang to age.

unknown: a large brown quadruped, white tail raised in alarm
behaviorDesc: Grazes with head down, ears swiveling. At the first wrong sound, the white tail goes up and it's gone.
huntText: It grazes, ears tracking every sound. The white tail flicks — once, twice — then it explodes into motion.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — this feeds people for days. Organs first (they spoil fastest and carry the vitamins), then gut and hang the rest. Don’t waste the fat.
tell: head snaps up — the white tail flicks, once, twice.
diseaseVector: Deer carry ticks — Lyme disease is real. Check the hide before you wear it, and cook the venison through.

name: Creek Chub
description: a small fish flashing in the water

knowledgeLevels.1: Creek chub. Small fish.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (eat whole if small), bones (careful).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: protein, omega-3. Good when other food scarce.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: tickle (hands under, stroke belly). Or dam and scoop. Best at dawn.

unknown: a flicker of silver under the water
behaviorDesc: Stays in water. Darts under rocks when shadow falls. You need a line, not hands.
huntText: A flash of silver in the creek. It darts under the rock before your shadow even touches the water.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mouthful. Eat it whole, bones and all, or the tickle wasn’t worth it.
tell: holds perfectly still in the current, fins barely moving.
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.

name: Wild Turkey
description: a wild turkey, iridescent feathers

knowledgeLevels.1: Wild turkey. Big bird. Wary.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: breast (best meat), legs (tough), feathers (fletching/insulation).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: high protein. Feathers are valuable (arrows, bedding).
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: call them (mimic). Hunt in fall (fat). Roost at dusk (find the tree).

unknown: a large dark bird, iridescent, head jerking
behaviorDesc: Moves in flocks. One spots you, they all know. Loud, big, but they panic in different directions.
huntText: Gobble-gobble-gobble. The flock erupts — wings like thunder, all going different ways. Pick one and commit.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the breast alone is a feast. Legs are tough; save the wing feathers for fletching.
tell: the heads jerk up in unison — all of them, all at once.
diseaseVector: Raw poultry carries salmonella. Cook it through — no pink.

name: Virginia Opossum
description: a waddling opossum, playing dead (badly)

knowledgeLevels.1: Opossum. Waddles. Plays dead. Hisses.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (greasy), hide. Gut carefully — scent glands.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: slow and catchable. Good trap animal. Immune to snake venom (irrelevant, cool).
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: trap near dens. They waddle into anything. Cook thoroughly.

unknown: a waddling pale shape, playing dead (badly)
behaviorDesc: When threatened, it flops over, tongue out, playing dead. It's not dead. It's waiting for you to leave.
huntText: It hisses, shows teeth — then flops over. Tongue lolling. Dead. Except the eye that tracks you. It's faking.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — greasy meat. The scent glands come out with the guts: cut wide, never nick them.
tell: stops waddling and bares its teeth in a wet hiss.
diseaseVector: Opossums rarely carry rabies, but raw meat is raw meat. Cook it through.

name: American Bullfrog
description: a bullfrog the size of a dinner plate

knowledgeLevels.1: Bullfrog. Big. Loud. Legs for days.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: legs (the classic). Skin and guts are not food.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: gig at night with a light. Legs fry like chicken.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: night + flashlight + spear. Aim for the body, not the legs.

unknown: something the size of a dinner plate, croaking from the mud
behaviorDesc: Sits at the water's edge. At the splash, it dives. You need to be fast or use a gig.
huntText: It croaks — a deep jug-o-rum. You step closer. Splash. Gone. The ripples are still spreading.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — it’s all in the legs. The rest is skin and attitude. Fry them like chicken.
tell: the croak cuts off mid-note. The ripples flatten.
diseaseVector: Frogs carry salmonella. Cook the legs through.

name: Eastern Box Turtle
description: a box turtle, ancient and unhurried

knowledgeLevels.1: Box turtle. Domed shell. In no hurry whatsoever.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (soup). Shell is a bowl when you're done.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: slow = catchable. But they live 100 years — take sparingly.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: only take what you need. Mark and release the rest.

unknown: a domed shape in the leaves, ancient and unhurried
behaviorDesc: It walks. That's it. It just walks, slowly, with total confidence that you're not a threat. You can pick it up.
huntText: It plods along, head out, utterly unconcerned. You could pick it up with one hand. It knows. It doesn't care.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — soup turtle. The shell’s a bowl when you’re done. It lived a century; take the lesson with the meat.
tell: pulls its head in a fraction. It has nowhere to be, but it knows you're there.
diseaseVector: Reptiles carry salmonella. Wash up, cook it through.

name: Gray Fox
description: a gray fox, climbing a tree (foxes shouldn't do that)

knowledgeLevels.1: Gray fox. Smaller than red. Climbs trees (wrong, but true).
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean), pelt (prime in winter).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: trap on trails. Wary — harder than it looks.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: the only canid that climbs. Check low branches, not just ground.

unknown: a russet-gray flicker climbing a tree (it should not do that)
behaviorDesc: It watches you watching it. Circles downwind to scent you. If you chase, it leads you in circles.
huntText: Amber eyes in the underbrush. It doesn't run — it trots, just out of range, looking back. It's toying with you.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean and gamey. The winter pelt is the real prize; flesh it carefully.
tell: stops mid-step, one paw raised — eyes locked on you.
diseaseVector: Foxes are a rabies vector — never handle one acting strange. Cook the meat through.

name: Rusty Crayfish
description: crayfish under every second rock

knowledgeLevels.1: Crayfish. Tiny lobster. Pinches.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: tail meat (small, sweet). Boil whole, peel tail.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: protein from the creek. Lift rocks, grab behind claws.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: night with a light. Baited trap = dozens. Purge in clean water first.

unknown: claws under every second rock
behaviorDesc: Under rocks in the creek. When you lift the rock, it darts backward, claws up. Grab behind the claws.
huntText: You lift the rock. It shoots backward, claws raised like a tiny boxer. Grab it right behind the claws — fast.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — sweet tail meat, a bite at a time. Boil, peel, repeat. The pinch was earned.
tell: freezes under its rock, claws raised.
diseaseVector: Raw crayfish can carry lung fluke. Boil them.

name: Raccoon
description: a raccoon washing nothing in the creek

knowledgeLevels.1: Raccoon. Masked. Hands like a toddler's.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (greasy, good in stew), pelt.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: trap near water. Smart — varies its routes.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: marshmallow bait works (they can't resist). Cook well; wash hands.

unknown: a masked shape washing nothing in the creek
behaviorDesc: Not afraid of you. Watches with clever hands. Might try to steal from you instead of fleeing.
huntText: It sits up, paws dangling, watching you with unsettling intelligence. It's not scared. It's assessing.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — greasy, good in stew. Wash your hands after; raccoons carry things you don’t want.
tell: sits up on its haunches, paws dangling — watching you back.
diseaseVector: Raccoons carry roundworm and rabies. Wash your hands after gutting; cook through.

name: Common Snapping Turtle
description: a snapping turtle the size of a manhole cover

knowledgeLevels.1: Snapping turtle. Dinosaur. Do not hand-feed.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: seven kinds of meat (they say). Soup turtle.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: jug lines with strong cord. Keep fingers away from the front half.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: tail-drag to move it. It can reach halfway back — respect the neck.

unknown: a huge shelled shape in the shallows, motionless
behaviorDesc: Does NOT flee. Hisses, lunges, snaps. That beak can take a finger. Use a stick, keep distance.
huntText: It hisses — a sound like a tire leaking — and LUNGES. The beak snaps shut where your hand was. Do not grab this.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — they say seven kinds of meat in one shell. The head bites after death: cut wide, bury the head.
tell: goes statue-still, neck coiling back.
diseaseVector: Reptiles carry salmonella — cook through. (The head bites after death: cut wide, bury it.)

name: Timber Rattlesnake
description: a thick-bodied rattlesnake, chevron bands, the tail a blur of dry sound

knowledgeLevels.1: Timber rattlesnake. The rattle means back away. It means it every time.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (good, tastes like tough chicken), skin (tough). The venom is in the head, not the body — but the head bites after death. Cut wide, bury the head.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: pin it behind the head with a forked stick, or take it at range. Never reach, never grab. Check sunning spots on spring mornings — they bask on trail edges before the day warms.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: rattlesnakes den together through winter — find one den and you find them all. Antivenom doesn't exist anymore. The System apologizes for this in Rev. 4.

unknown: a dry buzzing in the leaves, then a thick coil rising
behaviorDesc: Coils and rattles a long warning before it ever strikes. The one animal that tells you exactly what it will do, and means it.
huntText: A dry buzz from the leaf litter — a rattle, then the coil tightens. It isn't bluffing. Nothing about this is a bluff.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — tastes like tough chicken. The venom’s in the head, not the body — but the head bites after death. Cut wide, bury it deep.
tell: leaf litter shivers before you see it; then the dry rattle starts.
diseaseVector: The venom is in the head, not the meat — but reptiles carry salmonella. Cook through; bury the head deep.

name: Striped Skunk
description: a waddling stripe of black and white, tail up like it's making a point

knowledgeLevels.1: Striped skunk. The white stripe is a warning label. Read it.
knowledgeLevels.2: Spray: sulfur compounds. Blinds you for minutes, smells for days — and everything with a nose will know where you've been. Monsters have noses.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: box trap at dusk, approach holding a tarp low. Or don't. The meat is fine but everything you own will remember the decision.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: tomato juice is a myth — baking soda, peroxide, dish soap, that's the recipe. The musk glands come out with the guts; cut wide around them and never nick.

unknown: a waddling stripe of white and black, calm as anything
behaviorDesc: Ambles after grubs, waddles through your trapline, and does not run from you. It has exactly one argument and it wins every argument.
huntText: It turns its back on you. That is not surrender — the tail goes up like a flag, and you have about one second to reconsider your life.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the meat’s fine. The musk glands are the whole job: cut wide around them, never nick. Everything you own will remember if you do.
tell: a white stripe lifting into the air, tail high; the calm before the chemistry.
diseaseVector: Skunks are a rabies vector. Cook through — and never nick the musk glands.

name: Muskrat
description: a chunky brown rodent sliding along the bank, all purpose

knowledgeLevels.1: Muskrat. The little beaver that isn't a beaver. Everything a beaver does, smaller and angrier about it.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich, dark), pelt (warm, nearly waterproof). Lives in bank dens and cattail lodges; eats everything green near the water.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: set at the den mouth at dusk, or on the feeding platforms. It dives the second it spooks — chasing it is a losing argument with the creek.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: muskrats mark their runs with musk — the smell IS the map. Trap the run, not the water. Pelts prime in late fall; a winter lodge means a fat muskrat.

unknown: a ripple that isn't a fish, sliding along the bank
behaviorDesc: Builds bank dens and cattail lodges, marks its runs with musk. When it dives, it stays down — longer than you can hold your nerve.
huntText: A V of ripples slides off the cattails — then nothing. The muskrat is already under the bank, listening to your feet.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — rich dark meat, nearly waterproof pelt. The lodge-builder earned its winter fat; pelts prime in late fall.
tell: a sliding ripple line along the bank, and a sweet-musky smell on the water.
diseaseVector: Muskrats can carry tularemia. Cook through.

name: Wild Boar
description: a bristling wild boar, tusks yellowed, head low

knowledgeLevels.1: Wild boar. Tusks. Pawing the ground means it has decided about you.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich, fatty), hide (tough), tusks (tools, trade). Males are meaner; sows with piglets are meanest.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: from a tree or a trap. On the ground, a boar charges — 150 pounds of bad decision. Never chase one into the brush; that's where it wants you.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: it telegraphs — head drops, paws scrape, the snort changes pitch. Strike only when it's calm or winded. A charging boar commits: sidestep, don't outrun.

unknown: a dark bristling mass, head low, pawing the dirt
behaviorDesc: Paws the ground and snorts a warning when it notices you. Press it — or miss — and it CHARGES: 150 pounds straight at you. Sidestep, don't outrun.
huntText: It sees you. The head drops, the front hooves scrape — then it comes, fast and low, tusks first. This is the part everyone warned you about.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — rich, fatty, the tusks are tools. Gut it fast; a boar this size feeds the village for days.
tell: head drops, front hooves scraping the dirt — the snort changes pitch.
diseaseVector: Wild pork can carry trichinella — cook it through, no exceptions. No pink, ever.

name: North American Porcupine
description: a waddling porcupine, quills rattling softly

knowledgeLevels.1: Porcupine. The quills are the argument. There is no counter-argument.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (good, fatty), quills (fish hooks, needles, decoration). It can't shoot them — that's a myth — but it can back into you.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: ranged, or flip it with a long stick and go for the belly. Bare hands grab = quills in your hand for days.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: quills have barbs — pull straight out, slow, or they break off inside. Salt pork cooks out the wild taste. Winter porcupines are fattest.

unknown: a waddling dark lump, quills rattling softly as it moves
behaviorDesc: Ambles. Never hurries, never bolts — it doesn't need to. Turn your back is a quill-rattle warning. Grab it barehanded and the quills lodge in your hand.
huntText: It hears you and turns its back — quills up, rattling like dry beans. It is in no hurry. It has never needed to hurry.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — good fatty meat under the armor. Quills pull straight out, slow — the barbs break off inside. Keep a dozen for fish hooks.
tell: quills rise and rattle — a dry shiver of sound — as it turns its back to you.
diseaseVector: Low disease risk, but raw is raw. Cook it through.

name: Groundhog
description: a fat groundhog, whistling an alarm from its haunches

knowledgeLevels.1: Groundhog. Whistles when it sees you — and every animal for a hundred yards hears it.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (surprisingly good), hide. The whistle is the problem: it warns the whole meadow.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it sprints for its burrow the second it bolts. You get one chase — wind it before the hole, or it's gone. Traps at the burrow mouth work at dawn.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: after a whistle, everything nearby is on edge for the day. Hunt groundhogs LAST, not first. Late summer they're fat; spring they're lean and mean.

unknown: a fat brown shape rearing up, then a sharp whistle
behaviorDesc: Whistles an alarm the moment it clocks you — and the whole meadow hears it. Then it sprints for its burrow: fast, straight, gone down the hole if it gets there.
huntText: The whistle splits the meadow — sharp, twice. Then it's running, low and fast, straight for the dark hole in the bank. Cut it off or lose it.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — surprisingly good eating. Late-summer groundhogs are fat; spring ones are lean and mean.
tell: rears up on its haunches, nose high — listening for your next move.
diseaseVector: Groundhogs carry ticks and can carry tularemia. Cook through.

name: Canada Goose
description: a Canada goose, neck out, coming at you

knowledgeLevels.1: Canada goose. It does not flee. It advances. The neck means business.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: breast (big, beefy), legs (tough), feathers (bedding, fletching). A wing can bruise you; the beak pinches.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it charges YOU. Backing off resets it — it guards a patch, not a grudge. Strike when it commits; it telegraphs the neck-low rush.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: nesting season (spring) is the danger window — pairs defend. A goose that advances on you is protecting something; note where it started.

unknown: a big gray bird, neck stretched out, honking as it comes at you
behaviorDesc: Does not flee — advances. Honks, neck low, wings half-out. Back off and it settles; press it and the wings and beak are real.
huntText: HONK. The neck stretches flat and it comes at you, wings half-spread, utterly committed. This bird has never lost a fight it started.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the breast is beefy, the legs are rope. It fought you for this; respect the wings, keep the down.
tell: the honk changes — lower, faster — and the neck drops level with the ground.
diseaseVector: Raw waterfowl carries salmonella. Cook it through.

name: American Woodcock
description: a woodcock, leaf-litter made bird, long bill probing

knowledgeLevels.1: Woodcock. You will walk past ten of these before you see one. The leaves ARE the bird.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: tiny, but the breast is the classic. Hard to find, easy to lose.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it sits until you're nearly on top of it, then explodes from under your feet — you get one fast shot. Sweep likely patches at dusk.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: at dusk males do the sky-dance — spiral up, twittering down. Follow the sound to the singing ground, and you'll find them all spring.

unknown: leaf litter that wasn't leaves — a whir of wings from under your feet
behaviorDesc: Perfect leaf-litter camouflage. It sits still until you're right on top of it — then explodes upward in a whir of wings. One fast shot, or it's gone.
huntText: The leaves move — no, the leaves FLY. A whir of wings from under your boots, twisting away through the brush. That was a bird. That was always a bird.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mouthful of the classic. Hard to find, easy to lose, worth the one fast shot.
tell: nothing. That is the tell. The leaf litter is a little too still, a little too bird-shaped.
diseaseVector: Low risk, but raw is raw. Cook it through.

name: North American Beaver
description: a broad flat-tailed beaver, working the bank

knowledgeLevels.1: Beaver. The tail-slap is the loudest sound in the wetland — and your hunt ending.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich), pelt (the warmest fur in North America), castor glands (trade, medicine).
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: the slap means it saw you — it dives and it's gone. Strike before the tail rises, or trap the slide at dusk.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: beavers follow runs — muddy slides into the water. Trap the slide, not the lodge. And the slap warns every animal on the water: hunt beaver last.

unknown: a broad dark shape on the bank, flat tail dragging
behaviorDesc: Works the bank, always near water. The moment it clocks you, the flat tail SLAPS the water — crack like a rifle — and it dives. The slap warns everything nearby.
huntText: CRACK. The tail hits the water like a gunshot and the beaver is gone — just spreading rings. Every animal on the creek heard that. Your hunt is over.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — rich meat, and the warmest fur in North America. The castor glands are trade goods; the slap was the price of admission.
tell: the flat tail lifts clear of the water — the slap is already decided.
diseaseVector: Beavers swim in giardia water and can carry tularemia. Cook the meat through.

name: Bobcat
description: a bobcat, tufted ears, watching you with yellow eyes

knowledgeLevels.1: Bobcat. It is not prey. It is deciding whether you are.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean, gamey), pelt (spotted, valuable). Claws do the talking up close.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it circles. Backing away invites the chase; standing your ground bores it. Strike when it commits — miss, and the claws come out.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: it's an ambush hunter — it hates a fair fight. Noise, size, confidence: make yourself expensive and it picks easier math. Never run.

unknown: tufted ears and yellow eyes in the brush, circling
behaviorDesc: It stalks YOU. Circles closer each turn, yellow eyes fixed. Run and it chases; hold your ground and it loses interest. Strike true or wear the claws.
huntText: Yellow eyes. It doesn't bolt — it pads closer, unhurried, like it has already done the math on you. You are not hunting. You are being hunted.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean, gamey. The spotted pelt is valuable. It did the math on you once; it won’t again.
tell: the circling stops — it faces you square, ears flat, weight forward.
diseaseVector: Wild cats can carry toxoplasma — cook through. (If you're pregnant, let someone else gut it.)

name: Nine-banded Armadillo
description: an armadillo rooting in the leaf litter, armor clanking

knowledgeLevels.1: An armadillo. Armor-plated, snout down, digging for grubs.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: the whole body under the shell; the shell itself is not food. Startle it and it jumps straight UP — then runs for the nearest hole.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: real meat, poor man's pork, and it walks right up to you half the time. Corner it against a bank at night with a light, grab the tail — it cannot bite you from there. Cook it THOROUGH; armadillos can carry leprosy, and heat is the cure.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they follow the same grub trails night after night. Find the rooted-up litter, set a snare on the trail, and the armadillo delivers itself.

unknown: something armored crashing through the leaves at night
behaviorDesc: Roots for grubs, head down, deaf to the world. Startle it and it leaps straight up — a vertical jump that startles back — then bolts for the nearest burrow. Cornered against a bank or a log, it has no plan B.
huntText: A clanking in the leaf litter — an armadillo, snout down, digging for grubs. It has not noticed you. It will not notice you until it is far too late.
tell: stops clanking — a pink ear rises above the litter, swiveling.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — poor man’s pork. Cook it through; the shell makes a bowl if you’re patient.
diseaseVector: Armadillos can carry leprosy — rare, real. Wear gloves gutting; cook through.

name: American Crow
description: a crow watching you from a dead branch, head cocked

knowledgeLevels.1: A crow. Black, loud, watching you.
knowledgeLevels.2: Crows remember faces for years and tell each other. They mob hawks, owls, and anything else they do not like — loudly, for a quarter mile.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: stringy meat in a famine, but the real use is reading them. A crow racket that moves is a crow following something — a predator, a person, a monster. The crows know before you do.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: never hunt where the crows are watching unless you want everything in earshot to know exactly where you are. And when the crows go suddenly, completely silent — look up, look around, and get your back to something.

unknown: a black shape cawing from the treetops
behaviorDesc: Mobs anything it dislikes — hawks, owls, you. The racket carries a quarter mile and every animal in earshot hears it. Crows give you away. They also give monsters away, which is worth more.
huntText: A crow spots you and the cawing starts — three sharp barks, then the whole treeline joins in. Everything within earshot now knows exactly where you are standing.
tell: the cawing shifts pitch and moves — the whole treeline is tracking you now.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — stringy and dark. Famine meat; the feathers are the real prize.
diseaseVector: Crows don't give you West Nile from the meat (that's mosquitoes), but raw is raw. Cook through.

name: Bluegill
description: a bluegill nosing around a shallow bed

knowledgeLevels.1: A bluegill. Small, blue-flecked, everywhere in warm water.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: the whole panfish — fry it whole, eat around the bones. In warm months the males fan circular beds in the shallows and refuse to leave them.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: a worm on a line over a bed is nearly unfair. The small ones are sweet; the big bulls are dinner. Hands work too — move slow, pin it to the bottom.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: bed-fishing in the spawn feeds a village. Take the bulls, leave a few beds alone, and the creek refills itself.

unknown: a flash of blue-green in the shallows
behaviorDesc: In warm months the males fan circular beds in the shallows and guard them against everything. A fish sitting on a visible bed is a fish that has chosen not to run.
huntText: Circles on the creek bottom — bluegill beds, each one guarded by a fish that refuses to leave. You could almost reach down and pick one up.
tell: the circles on the bottom are fresh, edges sharp, a shadow hovering over each.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — sweet panfish. Fry whole, eat around the bones.
diseaseVector: Low risk — cook it through anyway.

name: Gray Rat Snake
description: a long gray snake coiled on a sunlit log

knowledgeLevels.1: A big gray snake. Rattler until proven otherwise — treat it that way.
knowledgeLevels.2: Proof: no rattle, no triangular head, no pit between eye and nostril. Rat snake. It eats rats and it wants nothing to do with you.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: good meat, cooks like eel. Pin it behind the head with a forked stick — it will musk and bite, but the bite is a scratch. Freezes when spotted, counting on you to mistake stillness for a stick.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: where rat snakes hunt, rodents run thick — which means grain, which means people were storing food here. A snake is a signpost. Follow the sign.

unknown: a thick gray coil across the trail — frozen, head raised an inch, tasting the air. Rattler until proven otherwise
behaviorDesc: Nonvenomous. Kills rats by wrapping and waiting. Freezes when spotted, betting everything on being mistaken for a stick. Grabbed, it musks and bites — but the bite is a scratch, and the musk washes off.
huntText: A gray coil on the log, thick as your wrist. No rattle sounds — but your hands do not believe that yet. It has not moved. It is hoping you walk past.
tell: goes utterly still — not a scale moving.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — cooks like eel. The meat is clean; the musk washes off the hands, not the memory.
diseaseVector: Reptiles carry salmonella. Cook it through.

name: Eastern Chipmunk
description: a chipmunk stuffing its cheeks, pausing mid-scamper to stare

knowledgeLevels.1: Chipmunk. Striped, cheek-pouched, quick. Half the squirrel's size.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: tiny meat (tender), no useful hide. The cheek pouches are the tell — it's carrying food SOMEWHERE.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it runs a fixed route — burrow to cache to burrow. Snare the run, not the animal. And when the chipmunks start stuffing in earnest, winter is close.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: never kill a chipmunk near its cache. Mark the caches instead — a chipmunk's winter pantry is a map of the forest's seed fall. You eat the map, not the mapper.

unknown: a striped blur darting between the roots, cheeks bulging like saddlebags
behaviorDesc: Darts in short sprints, pausing to stand tall and check the world. Bolts straight for its burrow when pressed — and the burrow is never far.
huntText: It freezes upright, stripes bristling — then it's GONE, zigzagging low through the leaf litter toward a hole you hadn't noticed. Cut the angle or lose it.
tell: rises on its hind legs, dead still, watching you with its whole striped face.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — two honest bites. The real lesson is the cheeks: follow a fat-cheeked chipmunk home sometime, and you'll find a cache worth more than the animal.
diseaseVector: Chipmunks carry ticks like everything else furry. Cook through.

name: American Mink
description: a dark mink flowing along the bank like poured water

knowledgeLevels.1: Mink. Dark, long, mean. It saw you long before you saw it.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: lean dark meat, and the pelt — mink fur is the trade standard of the north woods, warm even wet.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it patrols the waterline at night, nose down. It is a stalker, and it knows the ground better than you ever will. Box-trap the slide at dusk; it never takes the same route twice.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: mink go where the fish are. A mink on the bank means the creek is feeding — fish, frogs, crayfish. Hunt the mink's territory and you'll eat twice: once from the water, once from knowing where to look.

unknown: a dark ribbon of an animal slipping along the waterline, there and gone
behaviorDesc: A predator's predator. It hunts YOU with its eyes before you ever get a shot — tracks your movement, circles wide, and is gone before you finish deciding. Bold enough to stand its ground if cornered, and the teeth back it up.
huntText: You catch the dark slide along the bank — and then you realize it has stopped, head up, WATCHING you. It knows where you are. It always knew. Then it pours itself into the reeds.
tell: stops mid-slide, head raised, nose tasting the wind — deciding whether you are a threat or an idiot.
killText: About {kcal} kcal of dark lean meat — and the pelt. Mink fur is the north woods' money: warm when wet, light, worth more than the meal. Skin carefully.
diseaseVector: Mink run the same waterline as everything else — parasites possible. Cook through.

name: Great Horned Owl
description: a great horned owl on a dead limb, ear tufts up, watching

knowledgeLevels.1: Great horned owl. Ear tufts, silent wings, eyes like lanterns.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: rich dark meat, big flight feathers. The silence is engineered — serrated feather edges kill the wing noise.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it owns the night from a perch. Approach under cover; it hears a twig at fifty yards. If it turns its whole head to track you, you're made.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: an owl's perch is a hunting blind you can steal. Pellets at the base tell you what it eats — and what it eats tells you what's nearby. Read the pellets: mice, voles, skunks. The owl maps the night for you.

unknown: two lantern eyes in the dark above you, floating with no sound at all
behaviorDesc: Perches and owns the air. You don't hear it move — the wings are serrated for silence. When it decides you're prey rather than a problem, there is no warning. Just talons.
huntText: The eyes blink — once — and then the branch is empty. You never heard it go. Somewhere above you, wings beat without a whisper, and you are the thing being hunted until you prove otherwise.
tell: the head swivels the full way around, slow, and the ear tufts rise — it has decided about you.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — dark, rich meat. The flight feathers are silent-engineered; fletch arrows with them and they'll fly quiet too.
diseaseVector: Raptors can carry West Nile (mosquito-borne) and salmonella. Cook through.

name: Green Heron
description: a green heron standing statue-still at the water's edge

knowledgeLevels.1: Green heron. Small for a heron, hunched, patient as stone.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: good dark meat, long feathers. It fishes by standing still — and sometimes by dropping bait: feathers, bread, insects.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it watches the water, never you. Wade in from upstream, slow — the moment the neck uncoils it's fishing, not fleeing, and you get one strike.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: a heron standing at one spot, day after day, is a fish census. Where it strikes, fish run thick. Fish the heron's hole after the heron leaves — it did the scouting for you.

unknown: a hunched gray-green statue at the water's edge, neck folded like a spring
behaviorDesc: Stands at the waterline like a statue, utterly absorbed in the shallows. It barely notices you — until the neck uncoils in a strike faster than your eye. Explodes upward if you crowd it, all wings and outrage.
huntText: It hasn't moved a muscle since you arrived — and then the neck UNCOILS, a blur of spear-neck into the water, and it rises with a minnow wriggling. It is fishing. You are background.
tell: the folded neck starts to uncoil — a strike is coming, and it will not be at you.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — dark, honest meat. The long feathers are the prettier half of the kill. Clean it like a fish-eater: gut fast.
diseaseVector: Fish-eaters can carry parasites. Cook through.

name: Big Brown Bat
description: bats stitching the dusk, snapping up moths over the trail

knowledgeLevels.1: Big brown bats. They own the air at dusk — one bat eats a thousand mosquitoes a night.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: almost no meat. The value is the colony: guano is the richest fertilizer in the woods, and a bat roost means a dry hollow tree.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: net the flight line at dusk where the trail narrows. They're fast but they fly the same corridor every night.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: never hunt the roost, harvest the flight line — and only a few. A bat colony is mosquito control for the whole camp. One bat is dinner; a hundred bats are a season without fever.

unknown: something stitching the dusk overhead, too fast to follow, snapping
behaviorDesc: Emerges at dusk in a chattering column, each bat on its own erratic vector. Nearly impossible to track one — the flock is the defense. Lands only deep in crevices you can't reach.
huntText: The dusk tears open with wings — not one, a whole column of them, stitching the air above the trail in paths no eye can follow. Pick one. You can't. That's the point.
tell: the column funnels down the trail corridor — the flight line narrows, and for a breath they're predictable.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mouthful, barely. The colony is worth more than any one bat: guano for the garden, and a thousand fewer mosquitoes a night per bat.
diseaseVector: Bats can carry rabies — never handle a live one with bare hands. Cook through.

name: Eastern Coyote
description: a coyote trotting the trail's edge, pausing to look you over

knowledgeLevels.1: Coyote. Bigger than the fox, smarter than the dog. It is sizing you up.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: real meat (like lean pork), a warm pelt, strong bones. The howls at dusk are a pack roll-call — count the voices, know the pack.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: it learned your traps from watching. Move them, vary the set, or it walks around. At dusk it is bold; at dawn it is gone.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: coyotes are the woods' cleanup crew. Where they work, something died — follow a working pack at a distance and you'll find carcasses before the bones bleach. And a pack that loses its fear of people is a pack that needs to be taught it, fast.

unknown: a lanky gray shape loping the far treeline, pausing to watch you back
behaviorDesc: Circles, tests, learns. It watches your traps from the treeline and remembers them. The pack howls at dusk — and the voices move while they howl, so you never know how many there are. Bold when it's sure, gone when it isn't.
huntText: The lope stops. It turns, head low, and looks at you — really looks, weighing. Somewhere off in the dark, a second voice answers the first howl. You are being assessed.
tell: the trot breaks and the head drops low — it has stopped deciding and started acting.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — like lean pork, and enough of it to matter. The pelt is warm and the howls go quiet for a night. Gut it fast and hang it high.
diseaseVector: Coyotes carry rabies and mange — never touch a live one, and cook the meat through.
